resolutions.researcher_notes: Same PNGRB 13-Dec-2010 authorization letter as the Fuel unit. Subject line: authorization 'for laying, building, operating or expanding Agartala regional natural gas pipeline network as COMMON CARRIER pipeline network under regulation 17(1) of the ... (Authorizing Entities to Lay, Build, Operate or Expand Natural Gas pipelines) Regulations, 2008'. Body: 'The Board has decided to declare the Agartala regional natural gas pipeline network as common carrier with common carrier capacity of 0.50 MMSCMD ... in terms of the PNGRB (Guiding Principles for Declaring or Authorizing Natural Gas Pipeline as Common Carrier or Contract Carrier) Regulations, 2009.' Under India's PNGRB regulatory framework, a 'common carrier' natural gas pipeline authorized under the trunk-pipeline (Authorizing Entities to Lay/Build/Operate natural gas pipelines) regulations is the transmission-network category, distinct from the separate City or Local (CGD) natural gas distribution-network authorization track that PNGRB regulates under different regulations -- so this authorization type itself supports PipelineType=transmission. Single-origin (PNGRB) so tier medium. Value UNCHANGED; ref-only addition.

VALUE DISAGREEMENT, not a missing-source gap -- do not stage a ref for StartYear1=2023. PNGRB's Nov-2025 INGPL tariff order (pngrb.gov.in/pdf/orders/20251127_TariffOrder.pdf, confirmed via pdftotext -layout after url_verifier's large-PDF false negative) lists 'Chainsa-Jhajjar-Hissar' with 'Date of Commissioning: 27-03-2010' in its economic-life table (line 338), used there to set the pipeline's tariff amortisation start -- 13 years before GEM's StartYear1=2023. The order's volume tables also show it already carrying gas in FY2022-23 (1.78 MMSCMD, line 2933) and FY2023-24 (2.03 MMSCMD, line 3134), i.e. flowing well before 2023. resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE/ATTRIBUTION all confirmed. resolutions.researcher_notes: SPEC check on StartYear1. GEM carries StartYear1=1997 for P0925/HVJ. This is contradicted by every independent source found, all agreeing on 1987 (some giving 1987-88 to reflect India's April-March fiscal year): (1) GAIL's own 27.11.2018 tariff letter to PNGRB, Annexure-A para 1.1 (OCR-confirmed, see existence finding above): 'was commissioned in 1987-88'; (2) GAIL's own 2021-22 Sustainability Report Glimpses timeline graphic (same PDF as the Length finding, `pdftotext -layout` line ~165-167): 'India's first natural gas pipeline- Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) commissioned' positioned under the year '1987'; (3) Wikipedia's HVJ Gas Pipeline article (verified OK, contains '1987'): 'Construction started in 1986 and the system was commissioned in 1987'; (4) offshore-technology.com's marketdata entry (verified OK, contains '1987'): 'Commissioning Year: 1987'. Four independent origins (two of them GAIL's own primary materials) all say 1987, none says 1997. The likely explanation: 1997 is when the SEPARATE GREP expansion project was commissioned -- per the same GAIL tariff letter para 1.2, 'GREP-- Later, during the year 1997... the HVJ pipeline capacity was expanded... by laying a new 36" x 505 Km pipeline from Vijaipur to Dadri' -- and GREP is already independently tracked in the roster as its own row (P3297, Vijaipur-Dadri Gas Pipeline (GREP-I), updated 2023-07-13). It looks like HVJ's own StartYear1 was set to its expansion's commissioning year rather than its own. This is a genuine, fixable date error, not a judgment call, and warrants verdict=concern rather than a caveat.

GEM's EndLocation='Jagdishpur' is correct, but EndState/Province='Madhya Pradesh' is wrong -- Jagdishpur (the pipeline's own named eastern terminus, an industrial/fertilizer-plant hub in Amethi district) is in Uttar Pradesh, not Madhya Pradesh. resolutions.recommendation: flag Capacity=107.00 MMSCMD for Update review as a probable system-total-vs-segment mismatch, consistent with the same pattern already flagged on sibling row P0919 (DVPL-I) in this sweep -- do not silently pass
resolutions.researcher_notes: SPEC check on Capacity. GEM's Capacity=107.00 MMSCMD for P0925 (HVJ) is IDENTICAL to the value carried on all four sibling rows in the 35-row roster that make up the same integrated system: P0919 (DVPL-I)=107.0, P3297 (GREP-I)=107.0, P3298 (DVPL-II)=107.0, P3299 (GREP-II)=107.0. This is very unlikely to be five coincidentally-equal, independently-measured segment capacities; it reads as the SYSTEM-WIDE total design capacity copied onto every constituent row rather than each project's own incremental capacity. Two independent primary/regulatory sources corroborate the aggregate interpretation, not a segment-specific one: (1) GAIL's own 2018 tariff letter to PNGRB gives the incremental capacity buildup explicitly -- HVJ alone at commissioning: 18.4 MMSCMD (1987-88); after GREP: 33.4 MMSCMD (1997); after DVPL-I: ~57.3 MMSCMD (2004); after Upgradation Phase-I: ~68.3 MMSCMD (2010); after Upgradation Phase-II/DVPL-II: combined system total ~111.3 MMSCMD (2013) -- HVJ's OWN capacity, by this account, was never 107 MMSCMD at any point; that number only appears once every later expansion project is added in. (2) The current PNGRB monthly register's 'NGPL under Regulation 17' table lists the 'Integrated HVJ' asset (GAIL, authorised length 6,169 km) with Design/Determined Capacity = 107.0 MMSCMD -- an exact match to GEM's value, but explicitly at the SYSTEM level (spanning HVJ+GREP+DVPL-I+DVPL-II/Upgradation combined), not the HVJ segment alone. This is the same finding already independently staged on sibling row P0919 (DVPL-I) in this sweep, which additionally notes the figure is now ~4 points stale versus the current PNGRB main-table authorised/design capacity of 111.3 MMSCMD. I am not proposing a replacement number for P0925 myself -- whether Capacity should be split per segment (18.4 MMSCMD for HVJ's own historical increment) or consistently labeled as the current system total (111.3, refreshed) is a judgment call for Update, and is a cross-row (not P0925-specific) data-convention question. Flagging as concern rather than a silent pass per the sweep's spec rule that a source must AGREE with the GEM number, not merely mention the pipeline -- here the two sources found actually corroborate a different quantity (the system total) than what a literal reading of the column (this segment's own capacity) would imply.

resolutions.recommendation: Route to Update: confirm whether P0926 should carry a mixed/oil-primary commodity tag (or a companion GOIT entry) rather than a stand-alone Fuel=Gas GGIT row with a 5.84 bcm/y gas capacity. No matching 'Heera'-named entity exists anywhere in GOIT to absorb the oil share (unlike its sibling MUT, whose oil flow is already tracked separately as GOIT P5191 'Mumbai High - Uran Trunk Oil Pipeline'), so today P0926 is the ONLY GEM row tracking this physical pipe at all -- reclassifying/splitting it needs a human call, not a mechanical fix.
resolutions.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE is not in doubt -- confirmed via 3 independent origins: (1) India's Comptroller & Auditor General (CAG), Report No. 21 of 2016 'Union Commercial Compliance ... ONGC' (https://cag.gov.in/webroot/uploads/download_audit_report/2016/Union_Commercial_Compliance_Report_21_2016_full_report.pdf -- a 3.5MB PDF; url_verifier returns 200-but-'missing expected' on it, the documented large-PDF false negative, so I downloaded it and ran `pdftotext -layout` locally: 'HUT' is glossed in its abbreviations table as 'Heera Uran Trunk line', and the report describes it by name repeatedly, e.g. 'Crude oil from the offshore platform is despatched to Uran through two pipelines, Mumbai-Uran Trunk line (MUT) and Heera Uran Trunk line (HUT)' and reports a measured 3.09% MUT/HUT metering discrepancy for the Aug-2014-to-Aug-2015 period, i.e. both lines were flowing and being audited in that window); (2) Offshore Magazine, 'ONGC reports Heera-Uran pipeline leak' (2007-12-10, https://www.offshore-mag.com/pipelines/article/16797928/ongc-reports-heera-uran-pipeline-leak, url_verifier OK) -- 'ONGC has reported a leak on the Heera-Uran Gas pipeline in the Heera field ... This will lead to temporary curtailment of about 0.5 MMcf/d of gas to consumers from the Uran processing plant'; (3) the sheet's own cited ISOPE 1991 conference paper 'Design, Construction And Commissioning Of Heera-Uran Trunkline Project' (Jayachandran & Shiv Anand) -- I could not fetch onepetro.org directly (Cloudflare 403 on every route, including the resolved article URL, so it fails url_verifier and is NOT cited here), but its title/authorship/1991 date is independently indexed in a digitized ISOPE-91 proceedings TOC mirrored on yumpu.com (page 335, Vol. II) -- that mirror itself also fails url_verifier (paginated document viewer, no extractable body text), so it is not cited either, but it corroborates the paper is real and dated 1990/91, consistent with the sheet's StartYear1.

CLASSIFICATION is the real problem. GEM's OWN live ResearcherNotes cell on this exact row already says: 'Mainly a crude oil pileine but designed to "transport oil and gas"' -- citing that same onepetro paper -- yet Fuel is still set to 'Gas' and the row carries a gas-only Capacity of 5.84 bcm/y. This is a standing, self-flagged, never-resolved divergence (the standing-rules 'ResearcherNotes documents a deliberate GEM divergence -- verify, don't overwrite' case), and my independent CAG read corroborates the prior researcher's flag rather than resolving it either way: the CAG report treats HUT EXCLUSIVELY as a crude-oil trunk line -- part of ONGC's offshore-to-Uran crude custody-transfer/measurement chain, structurally identical to and paired with MUT (P0944 in this same roster, also gas-tagged, also missing a GOIT twin except MUT's twin DOES exist as P5191) -- with only the 'off-gas' (dissolved gas liberated from the partially-stabilised crude and separated at Uran plant) counted toward gas production after the fact. The 2007 Offshore Magazine leak report, in contrast, calls it a 'Gas pipeline' -- but the scale it describes (a leak curtailing just 0.5 MMcf/d, i.e. roughly 5 mmcm/y) is three orders of magnitude below the sheet's claimed 5.84 bcm/y (~565 MMcf/d) nameplate capacity, which is far more consistent with 'gas' here meaning a small entrained/associated-gas stream riding along a much larger crude pipeline than with HUT being a dedicated 565-MMcf/d gas transmission line. I checked GOIT (data/GOIT_oil_ngl_snapshot_20260810.csv) for a 'Heera' entry that could be the oil-tracker home for this pipe's dominant commodity -- none exists (only P5191 'Mumbai High - Uran Trunk Oil Pipeline' and retired P5192 'Bombay-Uran Trunk Oil Pipeline', both MUT-side, not HUT). So P0926 is not a duplicate of anything in GOIT or in this GGIT roster (checked all 35 rows -- no other pipeline shares HUT's endpoints/spec), it is simply the SOLE GEM record for a pipe that is, by the regulator-grade CAG source and by GEM's own prior note, majority crude oil. Recommend Update decide: reclassify/split, or explicitly document as a deliberate multi-commodity exception with a corrected capacity basis.

resolutions.pipeline_name: High Pressure Gujarat Gas Grid Network
resolutions.recommendation: No action required on existence/classification/ownership/location; re-verify StartYear1 if time allows.
resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, well-documented, independently confirmed across a decade+ of regulator publications, not a GEM-only entity. PNGRB (Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board) Public Notice dated 01.03.2012 (http://www.pngrb.gov.in/pdf/ngp/Notices/PN2march.pdf) names 'GSPL's High Pressure Gujarat Gas Grid Network' explicitly, tracing an application by Gujarat State Petronet Limited from an original 1120.08 km network (2009 notice) to an identified 2366.43 KM network, diameter 6"-30", system capacity 30.46 MMSCMD, design pressure 98 bar. PNGRB's own line-wise register 'Operating Natural Gas Pipelines in India' (15.01.2016, http://www.pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/NGPL-Operating-15012016.pdf) lists it as item 17, Gujarat State Petronet Limited, 2239.0 km, 31.000 MMSCMD, authorised 27.07.2012. The CURRENT PNGRB monthly register (May 2026, https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, printed p.2 'PHYSICAL PROGRESS REPORT OF NATURAL GAS PIPELINE', OPERATIONAL COMMON CARRIER section, row 13) still lists it as an actively operating asset: Entity GSPL, authorisation date 27.07.2012, authorised length 2,860 km, operating length 2,748 km, natural gas supplied 29.0 MMSCMD in May 2026 at 80% capacity utilisation. Independently, a March 2025 trade-press item (Business Upturn, verified OK by url_verifier, https://www.businessupturn.com/business/corporates/gujarat-state-petronet-receives-pngrb-approval-for-capacity-expansion-of-gujarat-gas-grid/) confirms GSPL is actively expanding this same named grid (new Anjar-Palanpur line, 274 km, 30in, connecting to the existing 36in Mundra-Arpar pipeline of the grid) to raise its capacity to 44.76 MMSCMD -- an independent, non-regulator confirmation that this is a live, currently-operating, currently-growing asset, not a phantom or a stale GEM-only entry. NOTE: url_verifier returned '200 but missing expected' on all three pngrb.gov.in PDFs (documented large/odd-encoding-PDF false negative per the tool's own docstring); I downloaded each and confirmed the quoted text locally with `pdftotext -layout`. CLASSIFICATION: correct. PNGRB authorises this under its natural-gas trunk/common-carrier pipeline regime (the NGPL register), not under the separate City Gas Distribution regime, so 'transmission' (as opposed to a distribution/CGD network) is the right PipelineType; Fuel='Gas' matches (it is explicitly a natural-gas MMSCMD asset in every source). DUPLICATE CHECK vs the 35-pipeline India roster: no duplicate found. The only similarly-named row, P0937 'Low Pressure Gujarat Gas Grid Network', is a SEPARATE PNGRB-authorised asset, not the same pipe under another name -- PNGRB itself lists it as a distinct line item (row 15 in the current report vs row 13 for the High Pressure grid) with its own authorisation date (19.03.2013 vs 27.07.2012), its own length (58 km authorised / 57 km operating vs 2,860/2,748 km) and its own capacity (12.0 MMSCMD vs 44.8 MMSCMD). GEM's split matches the regulator's own split; no merge recommended. ATTRIBUTION: Owner 'Gujarat State Petronet [100.%]' matches every source -- GSPL is the sole named entity in the 2012 notice, the 2016 register, and the current 2026 register, and the 2025 press piece is entirely about GSPL's own capex on this asset. StartState/EndState 'Gujarat' matches the state code 'GJ' in the current PNGRB register. CAVEAT -- StartYear1=2016 is soft: none of the PNGRB documents state a commissioning/first-gas year for this network as a whole; the only dated milestone is the PNGRB 'Authorisation Date' of 27.07.2012 (which per the sweep's own guidance is not a valid stand-in for a start year), and the 2016 date in the sheet may simply reflect the publication date of the 'Operating Natural Gas Pipelines in India, Jan. 15, 2016' source the wiki cites for Length/Capacity rather than an actual documented first-gas date. Since the network was already listed as fully authorised and (implicitly, given it appears in the 2016 'Operating' register) supplying gas well before that date -- and the underlying application dates to 2009 -- I could not independently confirm 2016 as the true start year and am not proposing a replacement; flagging for a future targeted look rather than staging an unsupported change.

resolutions.researcher_notes: STATUS/START-YEAR plausibility concern, not an existence concern - the pipe itself is real and PNGRB-confirmed mechanically complete (see the spec entry above). The problem is that this is a DEDICATED single-purpose tie-in whose only intended gas source is the Jaigarh LNG import terminal, and that terminal's own history makes GEM's StartYear1=2021 look wrong and the unqualified 'operating' status worth re-checking: (1) the terminal's FSRU (its only regas unit, Hoegh Giant) did not even arrive at Jaigarh until 1 March 2022 - a year AFTER the terminal's originally-announced 'March 2021' commissioning target (nsenergybusiness.com project page) - so no LNG could plausibly have reached this pipeline as early as 2021; (2) Hoegh LNG terminated the FSRU charter in April 2022 over 'the charterer's default of the contractual terms' and withdrew the vessel from India entirely (two independent LNG Prime articles, both verified live); (3) I found no report of a permanent replacement FSRU having entered service since; (4) ownership of the whole Jaigarh terminal project changed hands from H-Energy to AG&P Pratham around December 2024 (constructionworld.in, verified live), and as recently as the AG&P negotiation coverage (offshore-technology.com, verified live) the terminal is still described as a stake being acquired/negotiated, not as an operating asset. So for essentially the entire period since this pipe reached its full 60km (PNGRB shows that by mid-2024), its sole supply source has had no working FSRU. GEM's StartYear1=2021 reads like the terminal's originally-ANNOUNCED target year carried over onto the pipeline, rather than an actual first-gas date - a recognized failure mode (dating an asset from an announcement instead of an outcome). I could not independently confirm actual gas throughput either way (PNGRB's tie-in table does not publish the gas-supplied/capacity-utilisation columns that its main common-carrier tables do), so I'm flagging rather than proposing a specific corrected value - Delayed=yes/DelayType=confirmed IS well supported by this same evidence and needs no change.

resolutions.recommendation: No sheet change. Flagging so a future researcher who finds the original 2010 PNGRB order does not mistake its provisional figures (834.81 km / 4.0 MMSCMD common-carrier capacity) for an error in the current sheet values (877.86 km / 16.00 MMSCMD).

That letter states verbatim: 'the said pipeline project which has already been completed and commissioned between year 1991 to 2005' -- this directly and explicitly supports StartYear1=1991 as the start of that range; it is a primary regulatory finding of fact (based on GAIL's submitted proof), not a guess or an authorisation-date mix-up. HOWEVER the same 2010 letter also states: 'The capacity of K.G. Basin Natural Gas Pipeline network, length 834.81 kms, diameter ranging from 2 inches to 18 inches, is equal to 15.997 MMSCMD as indicated by GAIL... The common carrier capacity would thus be 4.0 MMSCMD*' (footnoted as provisional, pending final capacity determination). So at the moment of authorisation (2010) the network was 834.81 km / ~16 MMSCMD total capacity but only 4.0 MMSCMD DECLARED COMMON-CARRIER capacity. Every later PNGRB register edition I could check -- Jan 2016 ('877.9 km, 16.000 MMSCMD'), Feb 2024 ('877.86 km, 16.00 MMSCMD authorised, 19.4 MMSCMD design/determined, 864.90 km operating'), and May 2026 ('878 km authorised, 16.0 MMSCMD authorised / 19.4 MMSCMD design, 867 km operating') -- instead shows an AUTHORISED CAPACITY of ~16 MMSCMD (matching GAIL's originally-indicated total network capacity, not the 4.0 MMSCMD provisional common-carrier figure) and a LENGTH that grew from 834.81 km to 877.86-878 km sometime between 2010 and Jan 2016. I could not locate the specific intermediate order that finalised the higher capacity determination or authorised the extra ~43 km (candidate mechanisms: the 2010 letter's own final-capacity-determination clause, or subsequent GAIL applications not captured in these three summary tables), so I am not proposing a value change -- GEM's current 877.86 km / 16.00 MMSCMD is the value used consistently by the regulator for the last decade (2016-2026), while the 2010 figures are a superseded historical baseline. Treating this as a caveat, not a live disagreement, per the instruction to note material history rather than silently pass it.

resolutions.pipeline_name: Low Pressure Gujarat Gas Grid Network
resolutions.recommendation: None -- existence, classification and non-duplicate status are solidly confirmed.
resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, and unusually well documented. Four PNGRB (regulator) documents across 13 years all name this exact pipeline: (1) PNGRB's Grant of Authorization letter to GSPL dated 19.03.2013 (Regulation 18(1) -- the category for formalizing an ALREADY-EXISTING pipeline, not a new build) for '57.6 KM GSPL's Low Pressure Gujarat Gas Grid'; (2) PNGRB tariff order TO/09/2013 (27.06.2013) setting the initial unit tariff for 'Low Pressure Gujarat Gas Grid' / GSPL; (3) PNGRB's 'Operating Natural Gas Pipelines in India' list (15.01.2016), row 18: 'Low Pressure Gujarat Gas Grid network | Gujarat State Petronet Limited | 57.6 km | 12.000 MMSCMD | Authorized 19.03.2013'; (4) PNGRB's MIS Report for NGPL, month of MAY 2026 (current as of this sweep), row 15 under 'OPERATIONAL COMMON CARRIER PIPELINE': 'Low Pressure Gujarat Gas Grid | GSPL | 19.03.2013 | 58 km authorised | 12.0 MMSCMD | 5.4 MMSCMD supplied | 45% utilisation | 57 km operating | GJ'. A fifth, non-regulator document -- GSPL's own PNGRB Access Code Schedule-I filing (29.05.2018) -- independently corroborates from the operator side: it names 'GSPL's Low Pressure Gujarat Gas Grid' with real entry points (Shell, CAIRN) and exit points (NTPC Kawas, KRIBHCO, GSEC Utran, GGCL, Essar Power/Steel, GSEG, GSPC Gas CNG), i.e. gas actually flowing through named customers as of 2018. This is the rare case of an India gas row backed by primary regulatory paperwork rather than a press citation. url_verifier FAILs the content check on this URL (HTTP 200 confirmed live, but the tool does not extract PDF text at all -- it screens r.text against the raw response body, which for a PDF is undecoded binary/garbage; this is a systematic false negative for every PDF, not evidence against this one, and matches the documented 'LARGE PDF' / scanned-image false-negative classes in url_verifier's own docstring). Verified locally instead: downloaded and read with `pdftotext -layout` (text-layer PDFs) or `pdftoppm` + `tesseract` OCR (scanned image PDFs -- this document has no text layer). Same caveat applies to (1),(2),(3),(5); the 2026 MIS report (4) is additionally a large multi-page PDF, same false-negative family. CLASSIFICATION: 'transmission' is correct, not misclassified. GSPL is India's dedicated gas TRANSMISSION utility (distinct from GSPC Gas / Gujarat Gas Company, which are the city-gas DISTRIBUTION entities also active in Gujarat and separately owned in GEM, e.g. P0924). 'Low Pressure' in the name describes the pipeline's operating pressure class relative to GSPL's sibling 'High Pressure Gujarat Gas Grid' (P0927), not a distribution network -- it is authorized, tariffed and reported by PNGRB under the same NGPL common-carrier regime as every transmission trunk line in the register, not under India's separate City Gas Distribution licensing track. DUPLICATE CHECK vs the 35-pipeline roster: NOT a duplicate of P0927 (High Pressure Gujarat Gas Grid Network). PNGRB's own MIS report lists them as two distinct, separately-authorized assets with very different scale (item 13, High Pressure: 2,860 km authorised / 44.8 MMSCMD vs item 15, Low Pressure: 58 km / 12.0 MMSCMD) and different authorization dates (27.07.2012 vs 19.03.2013). Genuinely two separate regulatory pipelines under one owner, not a relabel or segment double-count.

resolutions.recommendation: Verify/correct StartLocation: 'Eklera' does not belong to this pipeline. 'Atakpardi-Eklera' is instead a named SECTION of the sibling High Pressure Gujarat Gas Grid (P0927) per GSPL's own PNGRB Schedule-I filing (gsp1209.pdf, p.2: 'Atakpardi-Eklera Section (HP network 2011-12): 43 mmscmd'). Recommend StartLocation -> Hazira (or the Hazira/Mora corridor) for P0937, and separately checking whether P0927 (currently blank on Location in the roster) is the row that should carry the Eklera/Atakpardi endpoint -- not staged here since P0927 is out of this pipeline's scope.
resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM's current Location fields for P0937: StartLocation='Eklera', EndLocation='Hazira' (both StartState/EndState='Gujarat'). None of the primary sources that name this exact pipeline mention 'Eklera' at all. The PNGRB 2013 Grant of Authorization (Schedule D) lists the authorized route as three named trunk pipelines -- '(a) Hazira-Mora-Utran, (b) Cairn-Mora, (c) PMT Connectivity to Mora' -- and Annex-1's section-wise table itemizes six sections, all anchored at Hazira/Mora/Utran/Kawas: Hazira-Mora (36in), Mora-Utran (12in), Cairn-Mora (24in), PMT Connectivity (30in), Mora-KRIBHCO (12in), Spur-line to NTPC Kawas (12in), total 57.6 km. GSPL's own 2018 Schedule-I Access Code filing for this same pipeline lists entry points Shell and CAIRN and exit points NTPC Kawas / KRIBHCO / GSEC Utran / GGCL / Essar / GSEG / GSPC Gas CNG -- again all Hazira/Utran/Mora-area, no Eklera. By contrast, GSPL's OTHER filing in the same gsp1209.pdf packet (pages 1-6, for the sibling High Pressure Gujarat Gas Grid, P0927) names an 'Atakpardi-Eklera Section' explicitly. The gem.wiki article's own prose ('The pipeline runs from Eklera through Attakpardi, the Cairn Oil and Gas facility in Hazira, to Uttran and Mora village') appears to have conflated the two GSPL networks -- it cites the same Grant-of-Authorization letter and a Gujarat Infrastructure Development Board (GIDB) page for that claim, but the authorization letter itself (verified above) does not say Eklera, and the GIDB page could not be independently confirmed to say so either: gidb.org has moved to gidb.gujarat.gov.in (301 redirect, both www.gidb.org and the new domain currently unreachable/TLS-timeout from here), and an archived 2021 Wayback snapshot of the original gas-pipeline-infrastructure page is a generic GSPL network overview (1,550 km operating / 350 km under construction) with no section-level detail and no mention of Eklera or Low Pressure specifically. Net: this reads as a genuine GEM location error, most plausibly copied across from the High Pressure sibling row, not a sourced fact about P0937. Not fixed here (see fills, marked UNRESOLVED) -- routing to Update per SOP since this is a value-correction judgment, not a ref-add.

resolutions.recommendation: correct StartYear1 from 2021 to 2019 (commissioned 14 October 2019 per GITL's own regulatory/credit disclosures) -- 2021 appears to conflate the pipeline's own commissioning with RFCL's (the sole offtaker's) unrelated urea-plant COD in March 2021
resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM's StartYear1=2021 does not match either independent source I could find. CARE Ratings' two press releases (13-Sep-2023 and 08-Dec-2025, both confirmed via pdftotext, verifier false-negative documented above) state unambiguously: 'GITL commissioned phase-I of the MBBVPL on October 14, 2019.' The wiki's own cited source (PNGRB's 'Partially Commissioned Common Carrier Natural Gas Pipelines', 31 March 2021 edition) only documents that the pipeline WAS ALREADY commissioned as of that March-2021 snapshot -- it is a status-as-of date, not a commissioning date, and 2021 is also exactly when CARE separately notes 'RFCL commissioned its urea project in March 2021' (a different asset -- the customer's fertiliser plant, not GITL's pipeline). The most likely explanation is that GEM's StartYear1 was set from the March-2021 PNGRB snapshot (or from RFCL's own March-2021 COD) rather than from GITL's actual commissioning date, which is a full 17 months earlier. I could not find a second, organizationally distinct source giving the specific Oct-2019 date (CARE's two reports share one analyst house, so I'm treating them as one origin for tier purposes), so tier=medium rather than high, though I'm confident in the direction of the correction given CARE repeats the identical date across two independently-commissioned annual credit reviews three years apart, each presumably re-verified against GITL's own filings.

resolutions.researcher_notes: This is the most material finding on the row. GEM's Capacity=78.25 MMSCMD for the 'Phase I' segment matches PNGRB's regulator table almost exactly (78.3 MMSCMD, 1dp rounding) -- but that PNGRB figure is explicitly the 'Authorised/Design Capacity' for the ENTIRE GITL entity/project (Authorised Length column = 1,881 km, i.e. the whole corridor, not the 365 km operating stretch). Two independently-sourced, organizationally distinct citations establish the actual built Phase-I capacity is far smaller: (a) CARE Ratings, in both its 2023 and 2025 press releases (same house, but each an independently re-verified annual credit review): 'The design capacity of phase-I is ~4.50 mmscmd [2025]/around 5 mmscmd [2023], of which ~2.02 mmscmd is supplied to RFCL under a GTA'. (b) Business Standard, a mainstream Indian business daily, reporting contemporaneously in July 2016 on the signing of the actual RFCL Gas Transportation Agreement (https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/gitl-signs-transportation-agreement-with-ramagundam-fertilizers-for-20-years-116071500658_1.html, verified OK): 'Under the agreement, GITL will supply 2 mmscmd of natural gas from Mallavaram of Andhra Pradesh to RFCL's plant at Ramagundam' -- an independent, decade-old, pre-CARE confirmation that the actual contracted/designed throughput for this exact stretch is single-digit MMSCMD, not 78. The mechanism is also independently explained: CARE's disclosures (and a related PNGRB/GITL diameter dispute, corroborated in a November-2019 APTEL appellate tribunal judgment I located via indiankanoon.org/aptel.gov.in but could NOT cite -- both mirrors failed url_verifier, one on a gov.in SSL certificate-chain error and one on a 403, so I am not proposing them as refs, only reporting what I read) state GITL built the 364.42 km Phase-I stretch at 18-inch diameter instead of the originally-contracted 42-inch, specifically 'leading to reduced capacity with respect to the authorised capacity' -- i.e. the smaller pipe physically cannot carry anywhere near the 78 MMSCMD full-system design figure. I am NOT proposing a replacement Capacity value myself (per the no-forced-numbers guidance and because 4.5 vs ~5 vs the CARE 2.02-contracted figure are three different granularities of the same underlying fact) -- this is a genuine value disagreement for Update to resolve, most likely by changing Capacity to ~4.5-5 MMSCMD for this Phase-I-scoped row (or by adding a ResearcherNotes caveat if GEM deliberately intends this field to describe the ultimate system capacity rather than this segment's actual capacity). tier=high: CARE and Business Standard are two organizationally independent origins, seven years apart, agreeing on the same order-of-magnitude, non-78 figure.

resolutions.pipeline_name: Mumbai Regional Natural Gas Pipeline Network
resolutions.recommendation: no change; add the two verified PNGRB refs + the GAIL network-report ref to Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Capacity/Length/Location/Owner
resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/OWNER: confirmed, strongly. The wiki's own cite #1 (PNGRB's 14-Mar-2011 authorization-acceptance letter, No.Infra/PL/Exis/17/MUM-REG/GAIL/01/11, https://pngrb.gov.in/pdf/ngp/Govt-Authorization/letter26april03.pdf) is a scanned image PDF (url_verifier returns 200/OK but can't text-match an image - false negative, not a broken link). I downloaded it and OCR'd it (tesseract, 300dpi): it is PNGRB's formal acceptance of GAIL's authorization to operate the 'Mumbai regional natural gas pipeline network as common carrier pipeline network,' addressed to GAIL's CMD, with an Annex-I table titled 'GAIL'S MUMBAI REGIONAL GAS PIPELINE NETWORK' breaking the system into two sub-networks: (A) Uran-Thal-Usar (Uran-RCF-Thal, Thal-Usar, Usar-Thal-IIL, IIL-H.R.Johnson, Usar-Khanav SVs), and (B) Trombay (Trombay-RCF, Trombay-MGL, Trombay-TPC) -- exactly matching GEM's StartLocation=Uran/EndLocation=Trombay. This independently confirms existence, GAIL as sole owner/operator, PipelineType=transmission (it is authorized as a common-carrier transmission pipeline under PNGRB regulation, not a city-gas/CGD distribution network), and Fuel=Gas. Not a duplicate of anything else in the India-gas roster: P0944 (Mumbai-Uran Trunk Line, 204 km) and P0926 (Heera-Uran Trunk Line, 80 km) are ONGC offshore-to-onshore trunk lines feeding Uran from the Bombay High fields, physically distinct from this GAIL common-carrier distribution network that moves gas onward from Uran/RCF/Thal/Usar to Trombay-area consumers (RCF, MGL, TPC, DFPCL). Cross-checked against the current PNGRB monthly NGPL-MIS report (data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, and the finer-precision 20250630 edition) -- both large text PDFs url_verifier flags as 200/OK-but-content-not-found (documented large-PDF false negative in this SOP); I fetched each and ran pdftotext -layout locally and confirmed the row by eye. Both list 'Mumbai Regional Network / GAIL / 14.03.2011' under the OPERATIONAL COMMON CARRIER section (not partially-commissioned or under-construction), i.e. Status=operating is current and correct as of at least June 2025 and May 2026. SPEC -- LengthKnown 128.68 km: the 2011 letter's Annex-I table totals exactly 128.68 km (19.50+20.00+20.00+27.53+20.00+6.00+1.20+4.20+5.50+7.70+0.05); the 20250630 PNGRB MIS report independently lists Authorised Length = 129.0 km (rounds to the same figure) as of 2025. Confirmed, exact. SPEC -- Capacity 7.04 MMSCMD: the 2011 letter gives declared system capacity of 3.542 MMSCMD (Uran-Thal-Usar) + 3.494 MMSCMD (Trombay) = 7.036, rounding to 7.04; the 20250630 PNGRB MIS report independently lists Authorised Capacity = 7.04 MMSCMD for 2025 -- exact match, two dates fifteen years apart, both from the regulator. As a THIRD, non-PNGRB-authored source I also found and skimmed GAIL's own 'Report for Capacity Assessment [of the] Integrated/Interconnected Pipeline Network' (a GAIL-authored technical filing hosted as a PNGRB public notice, https://pngrb.gov.in/pdf/public-notice/GAIL_Report_Annx_19042024.pdf, also a large PDF url_verifier can't text-match -- confirmed locally), which names 'Uran-Thal-Usar sub-network of the Mumbai Regional Pipeline Network (UTU)' and 'Trombay-RFC sub-network of the Mumbai Regional Pipeline Network' as components of GAIL's integrated system feeding/fed by ONGCL Uran, RCF Trombay, MGL, DFPCL Taloja -- independent (company-authored, not the regulator's own compilation) corroboration of the network's existence, owner and endpoints. CAVEAT (not material, not flagged as a concern): the current PNGRB MIS report's 'Operating Length' field reads 125 (125.44 per a June-2025 web-search snippet), about 3.2 km short of the 128.68/129.0 authorised total -- normal for these filings (a small idle/spur segment, e.g. the 1.2 km Usar-Khanav SV branch, can sit outside the actively-flowing common-carrier length while the network as a whole stays classified operational); GEM's LengthKnown tracking the authorised/built total rather than the month's flowing-length figure is a reasonable and defensible choice, not an error. Diameter is correctly left blank: the network has ~7 different pipe diameters across its sub-sections (26in down to 4in per Annex-I) with no single figure to report. StartYear1 is correctly left blank: the 2011 letter states GAIL's own completion dates for the underlying pipe 'are from year 1978 to year 1998' -- a 20-year range across many segments, not a single commissioning year; per this run's guidance, the 2011 authorization date must never be used as a StartYear proxy, and a blank field is preferable to picking an arbitrary year from that range. Net verdict: real, correctly classified, correctly owned, and both Length and Capacity independently corroborated to 2 decimal places by two dated instances of the same regulator's data plus one GAIL-authored filing -- tier=high.

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, well-documented, correctly classified. This is a PNGRB-authorised common-carrier natural gas transmission pipeline built by Reliance Gas Pipelines Limited (RGPL) to evacuate CBM gas from RIL's Sohagpur (SP-East/SP-West) coal-bed-methane blocks in Shahdol district, MP, to a tie-in with GAIL's HVJ trunk network at Phulpur, UP. Independent corroboration (5 separate origins, none GEM-derived): (1) PNGRB's own monthly regulator inventory (NGPL-MIS Report, May 2026 edition) lists it by name under 'OPERATIONAL COMMON CARRIER PIPELINE' #16, entity=RGPL; (2) RGPL's own operator website has a dedicated technical page for 'Shahdol-Phulpur Gas Pipeline (SHPPL)'; (3) a signed RGPL-to-PNGRB regulatory filing (Access Code Regulations questionnaire, 27 Jun 2019, RGPL letterhead) names the pipeline and confirms RGPL as the authorized entity; (4) Business Standard (independent press, 9 Jun 2017) reported RGPL 'laid a 302 km Shahdol Phulpur Gas Pipeline' connecting the CBM fields to GAIL's HVJ network; (5) CARE Ratings (credit-rating agency, Oct 2024 press release on RGPL's bank facilities) describes 'SHPPL's pipeline, housed under RGPL' in detail including FY24 utilisation and volumes. PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas are correct -- this is a trunk transmission line, not a gathering/process line (the RIL Gas Gathering Station at Shahdol is a separate upstream facility that feeds INTO this pipeline). No duplicate risk found against the 35-pipeline India-gas operating roster -- no other row references Shahdol, Sohagpur, or this CBM system. One data-quality aside (not a sheet defect): gem.wiki's own cite_note-3 (an EOI PDF at pngrb.gov.in/pdf/eoi/ng/eoi9/feb-14-EOI-9.pdf) is mislabeled on the wiki page -- the actual PDF content is an unrelated EOI (customer list totalling ~90 mmscmd, no mention of Shahdol or Phulpur), not the Shahdol-Phulpur EOI its wiki link-text claims. Not used as a source here; flagging only because the guidance says to verify wiki leads live.

So RIL's 100% ultimate ownership is not wrong as a fact, but the entity that holds the PNGRB authorisation and legally owns/operates the asset is RGPL, a step removed from RIL. An earlier company name for the same/related entity appears in a 2015 trade-press piece as 'Reliance Gas Transportation Infrastructure Corporation Limited (RGTIL)' -- 'the Gas transmission arm of Reliance Industries Limited' -- which received the pipeline license; by the 2017-2024 sources it is consistently RGPL, so RGTIL looks like an earlier/alternate name for the same corporate transmission arm, not a separate owner (kept out of the Owner field to avoid asserting an unverified corporate-history claim).

resolutions.researcher_notes: LengthKnown=312.00 km matches PNGRB's NGPL-MIS report 'Authorised Length (KM)' column for Shahdol-Phulpur (RGPL, authorised 11.07.2013) exactly -- 312 km. However, the same PNGRB report's 'Operating Length (KM)' column for this pipeline reads 304 km, and RGPL's own site independently describes 'SHPPL system is a 16 diameter x 304 km main pipeline.' Business Standard (2017, at commissioning) reported RGPL 'laid a 302 km Shahdol Phulpur Gas Pipeline.' So there is a real, well-corroborated 8-10 km gap between the AUTHORISED length (312, which the sheet uses) and the BUILT/OPERATING length reported by the regulator and the operator itself (302-304). This is not a sourcing error on GEM's part -- 312 is a real, PNGRB-documented figure -- but if LengthKnown is meant to track built physical pipe (GEM's usual convention) rather than the authorised/nameplate length, 304 km (the figure both PNGRB's own 'Operating Length' column and RGPL's technical description converge on) would be the more defensible value. Flagging as a caveat rather than changing the value, since 312 is independently sourced and the discrepancy is a documented authorised-vs-built distinction, not a fabrication or unit error.

Four independent origins (2 press outlets on one GAIL statement + 1 Indian-government investment tracker + 1 commercial database + the Lok Sabha reply as a 5th, government, origin) all agree this pipeline is real, GAIL-owned, common-carrier/transmission, and gas. DUPLICATE check against the full 35-row India-gas roster: not a duplicate of P0925 (Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur/HVJ), despite sharing the Vijaipur and Auraiya nodes — HVJ (commissioned 1987, 3,474 km, ends at Jagdishpur) has a compressor station at both Vijaipur and Auraiya per Wikipedia, but this pipeline is a genuinely separate, newer (2016-2022) parallel corridor that diverges at Auraiya toward Phulpur rather than continuing to Jagdishpur; it is explicitly described in sources as built 'to debottleneck the upstream network of the JHBDPL project' (GAIL CMD B.C. Tripathi interview, Indian Infrastructure, 2018-09-20), i.e. new pipe, not a relabel. resolutions.recommendation: ref-fill Status/Fuel/PipelineType/FuelSource/Location/Owner as below; correct EndLocation spelling 'Ramgahr' -> 'Ramgarh'; leave StartYearEarliest blank pending resolution of a real date conflict across sources (see notes)
resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/ATTRIBUTION confirmed via sources genuinely independent of GEM. Indus Gas Limited's own operations page (www.indusgas.com/operation.php -- Indus holds 63-90% of the RJ-ON/6 block over time, financing the SGL field) states: 'Within a short period of one year a large infrastructure development consisting of a dedicated 6" gas pipeline of ca. 90 km (owned by GAIL) connecting SGL Field with an existing power generation unit ... were completed and commercial sale of gas commenced ... GAIL has entered into a back to back gas sale arrangement with a 270 MW Rajasthan State owned power plant located at Ramgarh.' Business Standard (independent news outlet, 2009-08-07) reports: 'GAIL (India) Limited has signed a Gas Sales and Transmission Contract (GSTC) with Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Utpadan Nigam Limited (RRVUNL) for supply of natural gas for 160 MW gas power plant of RRVUNL at Ramgarh. GAIL also signed a Gas Sales and Purchase Agreement (GSPA) with the SGL consortium -- the contractors of RJ-ON/6 block.' Two NS Energy Business trade-press articles corroborate and add detail: the GSTC-signing piece states the pipeline is '90 kilometers long', '10 inch diameter', connects 'the RJ-ON/6 block to RRVUNL's power facility at Ramgarh', is GAIL-owned/constructed ('estimated investment of approximately INR1 billion'), and gas originates from 'the RJ-ON/6 block in Shahgarh, Jaisalmer district' (matches GEM StartState/Province=Rajasthan); the SGL-completion piece (as of June 2010) confirms 'Production facilities and pipeline completed and ready for operation', pipeline length '90 kilometers', operator GAIL, route 'From SGL gas field to Ramgarh power plant'. Together these four independent-origin sources (operator's own site; a national business daily; two syndicated trade-press pieces citing the GAIL/RRVUNL press release) confirm: Status=operating (real, in-service pipeline), Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission (a dedicated field-to-single-consumer transmission line -- not a gathering line, since it runs well outside the field boundary to an external power-plant offtaker, and not distribution; correctly classified per GEM's three-way PipelineType vocabulary), FuelSource=SGL Field (the SGL discovery/field within block RJ-ON/6), Owner=GAIL (India) Ltd 100% (GAIL built, owns and operates the line; RRVUNL/RJ-ON-6 consortium are the gas buyer/seller, not pipeline owners), StartLocation=Langtala and EndState/Province=Rajasthan. One correction: GEM's EndLocation 'Ramgahr' is a misspelling of 'Ramgarh' (the town/power-plant name is consistently spelled 'Ramgarh' across all four sources) -- recommend a sheet-side spelling fix, not a value change. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 35-row India roster: P1436 and P3905 (Dandewala-Gamnewala-RSEB Ramgarh Gas Pipeline) both terminate at the same Ramgarh power plant, raising a relabel/double-count question. Resolved as NOT a duplicate: independent reporting (infrastructuretoday.co.in, 2026, on a related ONGC Chinnewala Tibba announcement) confirms 'ONGC, OIL and Focus Energy Ltd. are among the gas suppliers to the [Ramgarh] plant' and that 'ONGC commenced gas evacuation to RRVUNL's Ramgarh power plant via its Gamnewala Gas Collection Station' -- i.e. Ramgarh receives gas from multiple, physically distinct dedicated pipelines from different fields/producers. P3905 draws from ONGC's Gamnewala and OIL's Dandewala fields (PNGRB-authorised 2012-12-14, ~65 km), while P1436 draws from Focus Energy/Indus Gas's SGL field via Langtala (~90 km, no PNGRB common-carrier itemisation found because it is a dedicated, not common-carrier, line -- consistent with the country guidance that dedicated/tie-in lines sit inside PNGRB's grand totals but are not itemised; confirmed by fetching the current PNGRB register, https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, and finding no 'Ramgarh'/'Langtala'/'SGL'/'Focus Energy' row). Different upstream fields, different producers, different lengths, different authorisation status -- two real, separate pipelines feeding one plant, not a duplicate. UNRESOLVED CAVEAT -- commissioning date: sources disagree on when the pipeline itself entered service. Indus Gas's own summary page implies the dedicated pipeline was complete and commercial gas sale began July 2009 ('within a short period of one year' of the March 2009 SGL Field Development approval). But both NS Energy Business articles (one covering the Aug-2009 GSTC signing, one dated to facility completion) instead point to construction completing Feb-Jun 2010 and full commercial gas supply beginning April-July 2010, with full capacity reached April 2011. Given this genuine conflict between an operator's own retrospective marketing copy and two independent trade-press pieces with more specific dated milestones, I did not fill StartYearEarliest -- flagging for Update to resolve (most likely 2009 was an early/interim gas sale before the dedicated GAIL pipeline itself was finished in 2010, but that is inference, not confirmed).

resolutions.researcher_notes: SPEC check on Capacity. GEM has Capacity=0.12 MMSCMD (CapacityBcm/y=0.04). Two independent sources materially disagree: Indus Gas's own site states GAIL committed to a gas off-take of 'around 33.5 mmcf/d (processed gas) under "Take or Pay" terms' under the August 2009 GSPA -- converting, 33.5 MMSCFD x 0.0283168 m3/ft3 = ~0.949 MMSCMD. NS Energy Business's GSTC article independently states the same contract explicitly in metric terms: the pipeline 'will transport 0.95 MMSCMD of natural gas for a period of 12 years.' These two independent-origin sources (company disclosure; trade press citing the GAIL/RRVUNL press release) agree with each other to three significant figures (~0.95 MMSCMD) and both conflict sharply with the sheet's 0.12 MMSCMD -- roughly an 8x gap, far beyond rounding or unit-confusion. I could not find any source supporting 0.12 MMSCMD specifically (not even the field's early, modest 7 mmcf/d = ~0.20 MMSCMD startup flow in July 2009 matches it). This does not fit the country-wide 'CapacityBcm/y derived from PNGRB's authorised MMSCMD' pattern either, since this dedicated line is not itemised in PNGRB's common-carrier register at all (confirmed against the current 2026-05-31 edition), so there is no obvious stale-authorisation explanation for where 0.12 came from -- most likely a straightforward data error. Flagging as a concern rather than a direct fill because Capacity is not blank on the sheet (an existing value should be corrected via Update, not silently overwritten by a ref-sweep fill).

SECOND independent origin: DNA India (2018-03-08 print report, live URL now 403s -- anti-bot -- but a clean Wayback capture from 2018-03-10 verifies OK): '...106-km captive natural gas pipeline from Dahej to Koyali at an estimated cost of Rs315 crore are the other projects to be undertaken by Gujarat Refinery...' -- independently corroborates the 106 km length, the Dahej-to-Koyali route, and is the exact source the wiki page's own infobox cites for its cost figure (Rs315 crore / US$42.6M). THIRD independent origin: India Investment Grid (indiainvestmentgrid.gov.in, a Government of India / DPIIT infrastructure-project portal, project ID 701295, page title 'Dahej-Koyali Refinery Natural Gas Pipeline Project in Vadodara, Bharuch (Gujarat)') -- independently confirms: Sector Oil & Gas / Bulk Material Transportation Pipelines, State Gujarat, Project Start Date 2017-08-03 (consistent with the PNGRB letter noting IOCL's application was dated 02.12.2017), Project Completion Date 2022-02-26, Project Status 'Completion Certificate/COD' (i.e. commercially operational), Promoter/Sponsor Type 'Central PSU' (consistent with IOCL, though the portal does not name the promoter by name in publicly-visible text), and Total Project Cost USD 39.61 mn. resolutions.recommendation: Update LengthKnown 815.0 -> 943 km (as-built/operating length, stable since 2023) and Capacity 19.90 -> 22.5 MMSCMD (current authorised/design capacity); route to Update, not auto-applied here.
resolutions.researcher_notes: Sheet's exact values (LengthKnown=815.00 km, Capacity=19.90 MMSCMD) are NOT wrong per se -- they are a verbatim, letter-for-letter match to PNGRB's own June-2023 edition ('Fully Operational Common Carrier Natural Gas Pipelines... As on 31.03.2023', archived at https://web.archive.org/web/20250523020537/https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/NGPL-08062023.pdf, fetched 200, pdftotext -layout confirmed locally -- url_verifier false-negatives on this large PDF, same documented behaviour as the current edition): row 6, PL Unique ID 17.05.NGPL, 'Dahej-Uran-Panvel-Dhabhol', GAIL, Auth. Date 10.05.2010, Auth. Length (KM) 815.00, Auth. Capacity (MMSCMD) 19.90, Operating Length (KM) 943.09. So this confirms GEM's numbers came straight off that report and were correct as of the 2023 update -- but the regulator has since revised the authorisation. The CURRENT PNGRB edition (May 2026, https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/20260531-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf, fetched 200, confirmed locally, same false-negative caveat) shows the same pipeline (row 6, 'Dahej-Uran-Panvel-Dabhol', GAIL, same original 10.05.2010 authorisation date) now carrying: Authorised Length 920 km, Authorised Capacity 22.5 MMSCMD, Design/Determined Capacity 22.5 MMSCMD, Operating Length 943 km, current monthly gas supplied 26.8 MMSCMD (119% capacity utilisation in May 2026, 108.4% on the Apr-May 2026 average per the Reg.17 breakout table). Two things follow: (1) CAPACITY is genuinely stale -- the regulator raised the authorised/design capacity from 19.90 to 22.5 MMSCMD, and real throughput (26.8 MMSCMD) already exceeds even that new figure, so this is real demand growth, not a units or transcription issue; per the country-scope guidance this is the expected 'stale authorised capacity, not a unit error' pattern. (2) LENGTH is the more interesting finding: the pipeline's actual as-built/OPERATING length has been ~943 km continuously across BOTH the 2023 edition (943.09 km) and the 2026 edition (943 km) -- i.e. the physical pipe has not grown in three years. What changed is only the paperwork: the regulator's 'Authorised Length' column moved from 815 km (2023) to 920 km (2026), catching up toward -- but still short of -- the as-built 943 km. GEM's LengthKnown field is documented as a 'Physical' attribute (docs/reference/gem_schema.md), i.e. it should track the built pipe, not a regulatory authorisation ceiling; on that basis 815 km understates the real pipeline by ~128 km (15.7%), and even updating to the current Authorised Length (920) would still be 23 km short of the stable, twice-confirmed Operating Length (943). Recommend LengthKnown -> 943 km, not 920 km, precisely because 943 is the figure that has been independently stable across two dated regulatory editions and matches the schema's 'physical/built' intent, while 'Authorised Length' is an administrative ceiling that visibly lags the as-built network. Tier=medium: both length/capacity readings trace to one origin (PNGRB), so this does not clear the 2-independent-source bar for a value CHANGE (only for existence, which is separately confirmed above) -- I did not have search budget left this session to chase a second corroborating source (e.g. a GAIL annual report or investor deck) for the updated 943 km / 22.5 MMSCMD figures; that is the natural next step before applying. Routing to Update, not applying here.
